title: The Alerj salary kickbacks ('rachadinhas')
summary: Rio de Janeiro's state prosecutors (MP-RJ) accused the then state lawmaker of collecting part of his staffers' salaries at the Rio state assembly (Alerj), in a scheme allegedly run by Fabrício Queiroz. In 2021 the Superior Court of Justice (STJ) annulled the case's bank and tax record searches, and in 2022 the Rio state court (TJ-RJ) dismissed the charges. The senator has always denied wrongdoing.
status: Charges dismissed in 2022 after evidence was annulled; a request to reopen the case was filed with the MP-RJ in September 2026.

title: The chocolate shop
summary: In 2019 Rio state prosecutors (MP-RJ) searched a Kopenhagen chocolate franchise the senator co-owned in Barra da Tijuca, pointing to the shop as a possible money-laundering channel in the kickbacks case. He gave up the franchise in 2020. The accusation was part of the kickbacks charges, dismissed in 2022.
status: Inquiry folded into the kickbacks charges, dismissed in 2022.

title: The Lago Sul mansion
summary: In 2021 the senator bought a house worth about R$ 6 million in Lago Sul, Brasília, with a R$ 3.1 million loan from the state bank BRB at interest below the bank's average rate, according to news reports. The Federal Police (PF) began looking into the loan terms as part of the Banco Master case. The loan was paid off early.
status: Under Federal Police inquiry (October 2026); there is no court ruling on the case.

title: The movie Dark Horse
summary: In May 2026 news reports revealed that the senator negotiated sponsorship from banker Daniel Vorcaro, of Banco Master, for the movie 'Dark Horse', about Jair Bolsonaro. He admitted seeking private sponsorship but denied offering favors or using public money. The production company denies receiving funds from the banker.
status: Case under investigation at the Supreme Federal Court (STF); no charges and no conviction.

title: His friend's betting site
summary: In October 2026 the Federal Police (PF) took to the Supreme Federal Court (STF) an inquiry into whether the senator was a hidden partner in BestBet, linked to his lawyer and friend Willer Tomaz; investigators say he had 'master user' access to an account of a holding company owned by Tomaz. The senator denies having a joint account or any stake in companies linked to the betting site; Tomaz also denies wrongdoing.
status: Inquiry opened at the STF in October 2026; no charges and no conviction.
